digest.component_or_area: dependency advisory gating and lane-specific CI response
propositions: A committed lock file freezes transitive dependencies, causing any published advisory against a pinned version to block CI on all in-flight changes regardless of whether those changes touched the dependency map

The Gerrit verify lane must block on CRITICAL/HIGH advisories only when the change touches dependency declarations (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, etc.), not unconditionally, to avoid punishing authors of unrelated changes
The scheduled main lane must fail visibly on outstanding advisories and escalate via ticket filing with dedup to route triage to the lock owner, not rely on a silent red

override-dependencies is the correct remediation instrument when an upstream cap blocks upgrading a vulnerable dependency; constraint-dependencies can only narrow and returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output, not proof of impossibility

The runbook must document the uv resolution mechanics (universal resolution locks every extra jointly), the distinction between real findings and DB-flakes, why recheck cannot clear a real advisory, and the evidence required before applying an override
